metadata.title: Nth Shelf Test95 — fresh Apocalypse regression and frame count
metadata.countingRule: Count each unique complete original narrative frame present in an actual pop-out once. Two frames in a crop count two, three count three, and so on. A complete frame inside a crop that also contains fragments may be credited individually; clipped frames, banners, credits and duplicates add zero. Grouping usability remains a separate issue.
metadata.inventoryBasis: Earlier 385-frame inventory rechecked against source pages and corrected to 384: issue 3 Reader 13 had counted a fragment of the continuous hand/wrist action as another frame. Covers excluded. Montage and borderless-frame identities are manual judgments.
metadata.verification: Fresh full detector replay of all 91 source images; all 186 descriptors identical to the saved Test95 checkpoint. All selections rendered through actual Reader.zoomToPanel and reviewed beside source; sampled findPanelAt hit checks record reachability. No runtime detector change.
limits: Local native canvas replay, not a fresh Android gesture sweep or phone latency measurement.
The count is for page-wide Test95 selections and actual Reader crops. Tap-dependent fallback searches outside those selections are not exhaustively tested.
The Test95 hand/water target has separate phone confirmation from Brad. Other page conclusions here are local regression findings.

Earlier credits were also rechecked: issue 3 Reader 12 S2 adds one complete frame; Reader 13 S1/S2 lose two clipped-dialogue credits; Reader 13 S5 adds one intact lower frame within a mixed crop. The net correction is zero. The old 171 count used the stricter single/exact-two-continuing-scene rule; the new count credits complete frames in larger and mixed crops as requested. A counting-rule change is not a new detector improvement.
Suggestions are hypotheses requiring isolated experiments and retained-regression checks; private artwork is excluded from git/CI.
